environment.runtime: single-process local Node runtime with file-backed JSON state
environment.data: isolated temporary DATA_FILE per level; private .data, fixtures and prior evidence untouched

workload.rooms: ceil(users / 20); the local runtime caps a room at 20 members
workload.ping: one WebSocket ping per connected user, staggered over the first 5 seconds
workload.broadcast: one host claim action per room at about 3 seconds; delivery measured to all 20 room sockets
workload.note: Polls and pings are staggered across the window rather than fired as one simultaneous burst. The intended 10-second window is measured client-side and stretched under contention; actual values are recorded per level.

reasons: Ping, poll and broadcast latencies exceed the local criteria
Ping and poll latencies exceed the local criteria

diagnostic.name: 500 users, polls effectively disabled (60-second interval), pings only
diagnostic.note: The 500-user limit is not caused only by the 2-second poll rate; the file-backed store, 10-second presence timeout and whole-database work on many requests also contribute.

conclusion: The local single-process runtime sustained 100 connected users for the measured 10-second window with zero errors. It did not sustain 500 or 1,000 users under the same workload. This is a measured local limit, not a Cloudflare Workers, Durable Object, production, 500-user or 1,000-user capacity claim.
changes: Added a repeatable local HTTP/WebSocket load harness (scripts/load-local.mjs and scripts/load-api.mjs) using isolated temporary data files
Added an idle fast path to LocalRoomStore.sweep so a read or heartbeat does not clone the whole database when no room is due; core and local suites still pass
